The text describes a telegraph hut located at a bore, a spot on a cattle route. The hut stood by itself, with no other structures around it, beneath a sky that was the color of brass. A single operator worked there, and his job was to keep the telegraph line open and functioning between the various stations along the run. In carrying out this work, he transmitted two kinds of routine information: he sent word of how many cattle were gathered at each water hole, and he reported on the weather, using short, brief wording to do so.

Beyond this daily traffic, the text notes a specific recent exchange. The day before the events described, a message concerning a rider who had gone missing had been sent out over the line. Then, on the morning the text describes, a reply arrived. The answer brought news of the missing man: he had been found, he was thirsty, and he was making his way home on foot, following the route of the telegraph wire.
